Subject: FintechCo  logging/redaction follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex / Sofia 

Thanks again for the call today  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard from FintechCo:
- You need request/response logging for troubleshooting and auditability, but logs must not leak PII.
- Specific items called out: account numbers, customer emails, transaction IDs that map to customer records, and any numeric identifiers (PAN/SSN should be redacted if present).
- Retention window: you mentioned 12 months for operational logs, longer for audit artifacts (7+ years)  we should confirm exact retention per log class.
- Residency: data for EU customers must remain in EU region; global traffic segmented by region is a plus.

What Redwood supports (high level)  see attached redaction-options.pdf for a compact matrix:
- Configurable redaction rules at ingestion (regex, header filters) to remove/mask headers and trace IDs.
- Token-level redaction for model inputs/outputs (we can mask spans matching configured patterns).
- Per-customer retention policies (Hosted default = 90 days; Dedicated/Private can be configured to meet 12mo+/7yr requirements).
- Traceability: we can keep non-PII metadata (eg request id, latency) for monitoring while redacting payloads.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You to confirm the full list of PII / sensitive fields and required retention per class (operational logs vs audit logs).
2) We schedule a short technical workshop with our engineer (David) and your SRE (suggested 60m) to review sample sanitized logs and validate the redaction approach.
3) Post-workshop well provide a one-page config + timeline for a pilot (Hosted or Dedicated depending on residency/retention needs).

Possible times for the tech workshop: Tue 11/30 10:00am PST or Wed 12/1 9:00am PST  let me know what works.

Attachments: redaction-options.pdf (matrix of capabilities and implementation notes)

Thanks,

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed PII / sensitive items:
- Customer email addresses and account IDs (internal numeric IDs).
- Any PAN fragments (we try not to store full PANs in logs, but need rules to redact if present).
- Internal trace IDs that map to payment flows (we want these redacted unless stored in an encrypted, access-controlled store).

Retention ask: 
- Operational logs retained for 12 months.
- Audit/evidence exports retained 7 years (we may export these to our archival store).

Residency: all EU customer traffic & logs must be stored in the EU region. US traffic can remain in US.

Sofia and I can share a sanitized sample log file (removing all real PII)  attaching fintechco-logging-requirements.docx that also includes our current retention policy excerpts and a short list of regex patterns we use today.

Workshop: Tue 11/30 10:00am PST works for us. Attendees: Alex, Sofia, our SRE lead (TBD).

One question before the workshop: can Redwood support header-level redaction (Authorization, Cookie, and any custom headers) and masking of trace IDs while still preserving a deterministic request id for cross-service tracing? We want to avoid losing correlation across services but also prevent PII exposure.

Thanks  Alex

Alex  great, thanks for the details and the doc. Quick answers ahead of the workshop so we can be prepared: 

Header-level redaction: yes  Redwood supports configurable header suppression and masking rules. Options include:
- Full drop: remove header entirely from persisted logs.
- Mask: deterministic hashing of header values (HMAC with per-customer key) so you can correlate without seeing raw value.

Trace IDs / correlation: we recommend deterministic hashing for trace IDs so correlation is preserved across services but raw IDs are not stored in plaintext. We can also keep a short non-reversible fingerprint for quick joins.

Payload redaction: we support both regex-based and schema-aware redaction (for JSON payloads we can redact by field path). For models/LLM inputs we can configure token-level masking and remove sensitive fields before persisting request/response.

Retention + residency: Hosted: default 90 days, can increase on request but may require Dedicated for 12mo+ and EU residency guarantees. Dedicated/Private: configurable retention policies by log class and region scoping (EU data remains in EU).

What well bring to the workshop: 
- David will demo the ingestion pipeline and the redaction rule editor.
- Monica will walk through retention/residency options and SLA implications.
- Well review your sanitized sample logs and propose a pilot config.

Attached is an updated redaction-options-v2.pdf with examples of header masks, trace-id hashing, and config snippets. Also adding a shared Drive link with a short playbook: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/logging-redaction-specs

See you Tue 11/30 10:00am PST  sending calendar invite shortly.
